item.title: Referee observer banned for discriminatory comments
item.description: [Getty Images] A Pro Ref referee observer has been suspended for nine weeks and fined £200 for making discriminatory remarks after a match he was working at. Brian Curson had visited Kenilworth Road to assess the officials at the League One fixture between Luton Town and Rotherham United on 15 November 2025. An allegation was made that Curson made two discriminatory comments in the lounge at Luton's stadium after the game, which led to the Football Association investigation. Curson was charged with acting in an improper manner and/or using abusive and/or insulting words. It was considered an 'aggravated breach', using words which included a reference - whether express or implied - to ethnic origin, race or nationality. Curson, who has been involved in football for more than 40 years, said that he did not recall making the comments but the FA commission "was satisfied on the balance of probabilities" that they had been made. The FA requested a time-based sanction because of Curson's role in the sport, as a player would serve a suspension of between nine and 12 matches. It was determined that, taking into account Curson's experience and role on the day of the match, he should be suspended for nine weeks. Curson was also told he must attend a mandatory education programme, and received a warning as to future conduct. item.title: Deion Sanders admits Colorado struggles: 'I'm just not getting it done'
item.description: Deion Sanders admits Colorado struggles: 'I'm just not getting it done' originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Colorado Buffaloes coach Deion Sanders acknowledged that his approach has not worked as he expected, taking responsibility for another disappointing season. But the heat continues to get stronger in Boulder. "We're just not getting it done" Sanders said during his weekly news conference Tuesday. "I'm just not getting it done. Don't say 'we.' I'm sorry. Scratch that. l'm not getting it done, all the way around. Offensively, defensively, special teams. All the way around." Colorado enters Friday night's matchup against No. 16 Houston with a 3-6 record. If they can win out, the Buffs will make an incredible turnaround. The difficult season for Sanders and his program has been a blur. Coach Prime: “The season don’t look good… I’m not happy with the outcomes. I’m not a loser by any means, and I hate the fact that we’re coming up on the short end of these games.” pic.twitter.com/s3O9L4JrSb — DNVR Buffs (@DNVR_Buffs) November 8, 2026 The Buffaloes are averaging 19.8 points per game, ranking 123rd among FBS teams. Despite the offensive struggles, Sanders dismissed the possibility of replacing offensive coordinator Brennan Marion, who is in his first season running Colorado's offense. "I love Brennan," Sanders said. "I respect the heck out of him. Some things we may just have to do a little different." Marion arrived in Boulder with an impressive offensive track record, having helped UNLV average at least 33 points per game since 2023. However, Colorado has struggled to translate that success into consistent production. Sanders acknowledged the disconnect, explaining that he recently addressed the team's scoring and defensive numbers with his players. "This don't work," Sanders said. "I got to do better. I got to do better. The formula don't work." Sanders has a 19-27 record in four seasons at Colorado, including an 8-4 campaign in 2023, a 9-4 finish in 2024 and a 3-9 record last season. Coach Prime also faces questions about his future, although a potential dismissal would carry a $26 million tab for the University. "We ain't thinking about no offseason right now," he said. "We're thinking about day by day, play by play, game by game." With the season slipping away, Sanders has made it clear that he believes the responsibility for turning Colorado around starts with him. After four seasons, the faithful in Boulder are becoming restless for changes. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Benson Boone to perform at NHL outdoor game at Rice-Eccles Stadium
item.description: Benson Boone performs "Beautiful Things" during the 67th annual Grammy Awards on Sunday, Feb. 2, 2025, in Los Angeles. | Chris Pizzello Benson Boone will be performing at Rice-Eccles Stadium on New Year’s Eve — and included in the ticket price is one of the most unique hockey games you’ll ever see. The Utah Mammoth will host the Colorado Avalanche for the Winter Classic on Dec. 31 at the stadium in one of the NHL’s annual outdoor games. That weekend will be packed with activities for hockey, basketball and music fans. Steve Mayer, the NHL’s president of content and events, gave the Deseret News a sneak peek at Boone’s performance, which will take place in the first intermission of the game. “We’re building out what will be the sort of his ultimate playground for him to do what he does best,” Mayer said. “He’s quite acrobatic, and he’ll be flipping from mountaintops and he’ll be running around on that track...about the entire stadium.” The track to which Mayer referred is a cross-country ski track that will surround the ice surface, given the large space between the hockey rink and the football-positioned seats. The stadium will be built out like a ski resort, as the Deseret News reported last week, and Mayer’s team is exploring the possibility of installing a ski lift or building a mountain inside the stadium. “He’s going to do a medley of his greatest hits,” Mayer said. “It’ll be 10 minutes long in the intermission. It’ll be and feel very much like a Super Bowl halftime in terms of how it’s presented.” Mayer also mentioned that there “could be a special guest or two” who join Boone. It won’t be Boone’s first appearance at a Mammoth game. He occasionally joins team owner Ryan Smith in Smith’s one-of-a-kind rink-side suite at the Delta Center. View this post on Instagram Boone’s Utah ties are plentiful. He owns a house south of Salt Lake City, as The Rolling Stone reported in 2025. His family lives in St. George, as KSL reported in 2024. item.title: Bizarre: these 5 managers and their crazy methods 🤯
item.description: Bizarre: these 5 managers and their crazy methods 🤯 Management genius or crazy ideas? In recent years, coaches' management methods have evolved enormously, sometimes involving unconventional ideas or an emphasis on extreme discipline. We begin this non-exhaustive list with the inevitable Mikel Arteta. Mikel Arteta and the pickpockets (among other things) Over his seasons at Arsenal, Mikel Arteta has become known for innovative and outlandish ideas to strengthen his team's mentality. Adopting a dog named "Win", showing montages poking fun at his players during training—but his best-known method remains the pickpocket stunt. During a team dinner, the Spanish coach hired professional pickpockets to empty his players' pockets. At the end of the meal, Arteta asked his players to check their pockets, and some discovered that their personal belongings had gone missing. With this idea, the Gunners' coach wanted to show his team the importance of staying alert at all times, particularly on the pitch. Guy Roux and the nightclubs During his years at Auxerre, Guy Roux revolutionised plenty of things, including keeping tabs on his players... quite literally! Eager to see his squad perform and worried about what his players might get up to away from the football pitch, the coach devised a very surprising surveillance system. " This was right at the start of the professional era. The players didn't know that the bouncers were also the people responsible for protecting referees at stadiums. So whenever players were there, the bouncers would call me at 8:30 in the morning to let me know, " he explained on RMC. Roberto De Zerbi and his training retreats During his turbulent spell at Marseille, Roberto De Zerbi attracted plenty of attention with his famous "ritiros". During these several-day retreats abroad in the middle of the season, the Italian coach took the opportunity to work on his squad's mentality. " I'd never done anything like that before, Jonathan Rowe recalls. I didn't even know it was allowed in football. We went to the middle of nowhere, in the woods, in the cold. We'd wake up at four in the morning and go running or walking through the woods. Then we'd do press-ups, a little strength-training circuit with torches in complete darkness, then another walk. Then we'd do hill sprints. De Zerbi would light a smoke flare and start marching as though we were Vikings ," Jonathan Rowe explained in The Athletic. item.title: How Jon Rahm's remarkable renaissance has set up Race to Dubai finale for the ages
item.description: Luke Donald may have had a little smile to himself when he examined the top of the leaderboard at last week’s Abu Dhabi Championship . The penultimate event of the DP World Tour season saw Jon Rahm come in from the cold to win his first event on the tour (excluding majors) in four years, fellow former LIV Golf exile Tyrrell Hatton finish second and Rory McIlroy come home third. Three of European Ryder Cup captain Donald’s most important players dominating one of their home tour’s biggest events – with the promise of more battles to come over the next 10 months before the 2027 showdown with the US at Adare Manor – bodes awfully well. It’s an exciting time for the DP World Tour, with the demise of LIV Golf meaning that many of the sport’s big names, from both Europe and overseas, who would otherwise be playing elsewhere next year will be plying their trade on the circuit formerly known as the European Tour. A rejuvenated Jon Rahm won in Abu Dhabi last week (AP) Leaderboards as star-studded as the Abu Dhabi Championship will become more commonplace, attracting more eyeballs to the tour and giving homegrown players a much more regular taste of elite competition. In that vein, this week’s $10m DP World Tour Championship at the Earth Course in Dubai could be the most exciting finale to the Race to Dubai – the tour’s season-long order of merit – for many years. McIlroy vs Rahm vs Eugenio Chacarra vs Patrick Reed vs Aaron Rai vs Ryan Fox . It has the perfect blend of global superstars who are in good form (Rahm and McIlroy), two more recent major winners (Rai and Fox), a pantomime villain (Reed) and an up-and-coming European talent who has had a superb season and is now trying to hold off the big horses charging from behind (Chacarra). And if you have a soft spot true outsiders, you’ll be pleased to know that even Casey Jarvis, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier still have a mathematical chance of taking the crown should they win the tournament and other results fall in their favour – making it a nine-way battle. Seven-time Race to Dubai winner (including each of the last four) McIlroy must be the favourite, with only he and the much more unproven Chacarra being in the enviable position of knowing that winning the DP World Tour Championship guarantees victory in the order of merit regardless of everyone else’s results. The Northern Irishman will also match Colin Montgomerie for the all-time record of eight if he gets over the line this weekend. item.title: Former Steelers player, coach Dick Hoak dies at 86
item.description: PITTSBURGH - 2005: Dick Hoak of the Pittsburgh Steelers poses for his 2005 NFL headshot at photo day in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Getty Images) NFL Photos/Getty Images Dick Hoak , who spent decades with the Pittsburgh Steelers as a player and coach, has died at the age of 86. Steelers President Art Rooney II announced his death on Wednesday, saying, “We are deeply saddened by the passing of Dick Hoak, a legendary member of the Pittsburgh Steelers family. Dick was part of the foundation of this organization and played an instrumental role in shaping the Steelers as both a player and coach during his 45 years with the team.” Hoak, from Jeannette, was a running back from 1961-1970, still remaining seventh on the franchise’s all-time rushing list with 3,965 yards. “Dick represented everything the Steelers stand for with his toughness, loyalty, dedication and an unwavering commitment to the team. First as a player, then as a coach, Dick’s contributions to this organization spanned generations,” Rooney said. Hoak then served as a running backs coach for the Steelers from 1972-2007, both under Chuck Noll and Bill Cowher. “He was respected and admired by everyone who had the privilege of knowing and working with him. His legacy includes coaching some of the all-time great Steelers, including Franco Harris, Rocky Bleier, Jerome Bettis, and Willie Parker,” Rooney said. “Our thoughts and prayers are with the entire Hoak family during this difficult time. item.description: FILE - Pittsburgh Steelers running backs coach Dick Hoak, in his 34th season as a Steelers assistant coach, talks with running back Verron Haynes before a team workout at the Pontiac Silverdom, Feb. 1, 2006 in Pontiac, Mich. (AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar, File) Longtime Pittsburgh Steelers running back and coach and five-time Super Bowl champion Dick Hoak has died at the age of 86, the team announced on Wednesday. Hoak, a Jeannette native and Penn State alum, first joined the Steelers as a seventh-round draft pick in the 1961 NFL Draft. In a period of turmoil and struggle for the team, Hoak was one of the most consistent contributors over his 10-year career as a running back. He started at least seven games in eight of his 10 seasons, beginning in his rookie year in 1961. Hoak’s best season came in 1968, when he had 858 yards and also added 253 receiving yards. When he retired after the 1970 season, Hoak was second on the team’s all-time rushing list with 3,965 yards, and he remains eighth all-time in team history. item.title: Before the NFL was big, Lions players served their country in big ways
item.description: As much as any professional sports league in America, the National Football League uses its huge public platform to honor service members, veterans and military families. In fact, as part of the NFL’s annual “Salute to Service” initiative throughout November, during Weeks 9-11 of the regular season, all 32 NFL teams will recognize the military community through game day tributes, community events and charitable initiatives that build on the league's year-round commitment to those who serve. On Sunday, Nov. 22, the Detroit Lions will host their Salute to Service game for 2026 when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers visit Ford Field. The special ceremonies will include the National Anthem sung by Detroit native and US Air Force Staff Sergeant MeLan Kameyo Smartt; a giant U.S. flag presentation, including a group of military veterans that are longtime Lions fans; a $25,000 Folds of Honor Scholarship Check presented to a local community hero; recognition of Lions special teams coordinator Dave Fipp as the team’s nominee for the NFL’s 2026 Salute To Service Award; and more. However, before that game, the observance of Veterans Day on Nov. 11 provides an opportunity to reflect back on a time before professional football was “America’s passion," but was instead played by young men with boundless passion not just for the game, but also for their country. A product of those times with a connection to the Lions, was Dave Schreiner, who was celebrated in newspapers across the country, including the Detroit Free Press, when he was voted the Big Ten’s “Player of the Year” in 1942 as the first two-time All Big Ten selection for the University of Wisconsin, where he played end. item.description: Mizzou soccer has named its third head coach in program history. The Tigers announced Tuesday night that they have hired Stanford associated head coach Paul Hart to lead the Mizzou program beginning in the 2027 season. Hart will replace Stefanie Golan , who was the head coach in Columbia for the past six seasons. "I'm incredibly honored and excited to become the head coach at the University of Missouri ," Hart said in a news release. "Mizzou is a special place, with a tremendous university and a commitment to competing at the highest level. I'm grateful to Laird Veatch and Angie Jabir and everyone involved in this process. I'm eager to get to Columbia, build relationships with our student-athletes and begin the work of leading a program that our university and community will be proud to support. We have high expectations, and I'm excited about what we can accomplish together." According to the news release, Hart has agreed to a five-year contract with Missouri. The terms of that contract were not immediately available. Hart will remain with the Cardinal through the end of their season. Stanford finished the regular season with an 11-4-2 record and are expected to make the NCAA Tournament field, which will be announced Nov. 16. He worked under longtime Stanford head coach Paul Ratcliffe for the past six seasons. The Cardinal were the national runner-up in both 2023 and 2025 and made it to the Women’s College Cup semifinals in 2024. Hart is a London native who played college soccer at West Texas A&M, where he won the Lone Star Conference’s Goalkeeper of the Year honors for four straight years. He spent three years with Queens Park Rangers’ academy in England in the mid-1990s. Before joining Stanford, where he was promoted to associate head coach after the 2025 season, Hart spent time as an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator at Washington, Oklahoma and San Francisco. He began his coaching career as the goalkeepers coach at UC Santa Barbara. Hart will be the third head coach in program history. item.title: Ceará bid to avoid unprecedented relegation as 2025 scenario repeats
item.description: Ceará bid to avoid unprecedented relegation as 2025 scenario repeats Ceará went into the 35th round of last year's Brasileirão with 42 points. They needed just three more to avoid relegation, with 12 still available. But they picked up only one against the four teams then in the top four (Mirassol, Cruzeiro, Flamengo and Palmeiras) and ended up relegated. They spent only the final half-hour of the season in the relegation zone, but that was enough to seal an unlikely drop. Now the situation for the black-and-white side from Porangabuçu is even more dramatic. Their mission against CRB next Saturday (14) is to avoid something unprecedented: relegation to Brazil's Série C. Favorites failed to deliver... Ceará actually made a positive start to the current Série B campaign, sitting sixth after six rounds and still unbeaten. It suggested they would challenge for an automatic promotion spot to Série A, or at least a place in the playoffs. That would have justified having one of the four biggest wage bills in the competition. Instead, they entered the closing stages battling relegation. They did rally, taking 11 of a possible 15 points between rounds 28 and 32 to move closer to safety. But then they got themselves into trouble: one draw and four defeats. Last Sunday's (8) defeat at home at Castelão to already-relegated América Mineiro also prompted coach Daniel Paulista to resign. And it left Vozão in a precarious position. The risk was just 1%... Before facing América Mineiro, Ceará were still in a comfortable position. They had lost to Athletic, but needed just one point from the remaining six to turn their attention fully to 2027. At that point, their mathematical chance of relegation was 1%, according to the Mathematics Department at the Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG). But defeat to another team from Minas Gerais left them in their current predicament. Their fate is still in their own hands, but the risk of relegation stands at 19.3%, and the situation is far from straightforward. They need at least a point against CRB at Rei Pelé to avoid a first-ever drop to the third tier. They have 43 points and 11 wins, sitting in 16th place. Avaí are just behind them on 40 points, with the same number of wins. The catch is that Vozão will be away to the team currently in sixth, who also have their fate in their own hands as they look to secure the final playoff spot. Avaí, meanwhile, will face Ceará's latest conquerors in Belo Horizonte. A defeat to CRB combined with an Avaí win would relegate Ceará.
